summary:
AURORA-X (Autonomous Unified Risk Orchestration & Adaptive Intelligence) is an AI-powered, offline-first astronaut health and cognitive-risk intelligence system designed for long-duration deep-space missions.

We developed a prototype featuring two operating modes: Helmet Mode, which simulates EEG monitoring through a proposed helmet-integrated sensor system without requiring a separate wearable headband, and Cabin Mode, which analyses available spacecraft medical, environmental, sleep, workload and mission data without additional wearable devices.

Our system combines EEG signal preprocessing, artifact filtering, a Data Confidence Engine and a Predictive Cross-Domain Risk Engine covering seven interconnected domains: physiological, sleep, workload, environment, neuro-cognitive, hydration and radiation. It identifies potential risk patterns, provides explainable assessments and prioritizes alerts while protecting critical safety notifications.

AURORA-X addresses the challenge of monitoring astronaut health and cognitive performance in isolated deep-space environments with limited communication and practical hardware constraints. It is important because early risk awareness and intelligent decision support can help protect astronaut well-being, maintain mission focus and support safer long-duration space exploration.
details:
AURORA-X – Project Details

AURORA-X (Autonomous Unified Risk Orchestration & Adaptive Intelligence) is an AI-powered, offline-first astronaut health and cognitive-risk monitoring system designed to support astronauts during long-duration deep-space missions.

How It Works

AURORA-X collects and analyses multiple categories of mission-related information, including physiological data, sleep patterns, workload, cabin environmental conditions, hydration status and radiation exposure. It uses a Data Confidence Engine to assess the reliability, quality and completeness of incoming data before passing it to the Predictive Cross-Domain Risk Engine.

The system has two operating modes:

  • Helmet Mode: Explores EEG monitoring through a proposed sensor system integrated into the astronaut's existing helmet, avoiding a separate wearable headband. The prototype uses simulated or uploaded EEG signals to demonstrate artifact filtering, feature extraction and cognitive workload assessment.
  • Cabin Mode: Estimates potential cognitive-performance risks using available or simulated spacecraft medical telemetry, environmental readings, sleep schedules, workload information, radiation records and short cognitive check-ins. It does not claim to measure brain activity without EEG sensors.

The system identifies potential risk patterns, provides explainable alerts and recommends appropriate actions, such as rest or workload adjustments. Critical safety alerts are always preserved, while only non-critical notifications may be temporarily suppressed to reduce cognitive overload.

Benefits and Intended Impact

AURORA-X aims to improve astronaut health awareness, reduce information overload, support early identification of potential risks and help maintain mission focus. Its offline-first design is intended to support operation in communication-limited environments. It can also help mission teams understand how interacting factors such as poor sleep, radiation exposure, environmental changes and demanding tasks may affect astronaut performance.

Technology Used

The prototype technology stack includes:

  • Programming language: Python
  • Application framework: Streamlit
  • Machine learning: Scikit-learn
  • Data processing: Pandas and NumPy
  • Database: SQLite
  • Visualization: Plotly
  • Quantum computing research: Qiskit and PennyLane for simulated quantum machine learning experiments

The prototype uses synthetic or public benchmark EEG signals and simulated mission data. It does not use flight-certified hardware or actual astronaut medical data.

Creativity and Innovation

The creative aspect of AURORA-X is its confidence-aware, cross-domain approach to astronaut health intelligence. Instead of analysing each risk independently, it considers how multiple factors can interact. Its proposed helmet-integrated EEG concept avoids requiring astronauts to wear a separate headband. The two operating modes also allow the software concept to demonstrate risk assessment both when EEG input is available and when astronauts are in the cabin without a helmet.

A hybrid classical machine-learning and quantum-ready architecture provides a foundation for future research into complex multi-domain correlations. Quantum machine learning remains experimental and is evaluated through classical simulators; no quantum performance advantage is claimed.

Factors Considered

Our team considered astronaut comfort, limited hardware availability, communication constraints, data reliability, sensor noise, privacy, cognitive workload, alert prioritization, operational safety and the limitations of simulated data. AURORA-X is designed as a decision-support prototype, not a medical diagnostic system, and does not replace flight surgeons or established spacecraft safety procedures.
